subject.title: Feature Request: Voice Recognition / Speaker Identification for Voice Interface

question: Should OpenClaw add enrolled-speaker filtering to the native live voice interface, and if so should it live in core native voice code or behind a new plugin/provider API seam?
rationale: The request is not a narrow bug fix: it changes who can trigger commands, may store voice profiles, and needs ownership choices across native apps, Talk providers, config/schema, storage, and fallback behavior.

options.title: Design core/API seam first
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a product/security design that defines enrollment storage, matching policy, fallback behavior, and whether plugins/providers can own the speaker-verification implementation.

options.title: Move to plugin-only exploration
options.body: Ask for an external plugin or ClawHub proof only if maintainers confirm current or planned plugin APIs can safely gate live voice input before transcripts reach sessions.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Reject enrolled-speaker filtering for now if the privacy, biometric-storage, platform, or maintenance cost is outside current voice-interface scope.

recommendation.title: Design core/API seam first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a product/security design that defines enrollment storage, matching policy, fallback behavior, and whether plugins/providers can own the speaker-verification implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: History shows the broadest recent ownership of the Voice Wake/Talk runtime and config surfaces that would need the product/API decision.
